publication_guidance.purpose: Bibliographic and rights-review metadata for the PDFs in this directory.
publication_guidance.important: This metadata is not legal advice and does not grant permission to redistribute any work.
publication_guidance.public_directory_warning: Files under Next.js public/ are directly accessible over the web. A rights warning in this JSON does not restrict access to a PDF.
publication_guidance.cover_thumbnail_policy: The site shows only small, low-resolution first-page previews for resources whose cover image is cleared for non-commercial educational use. Resources with unresolved cover-image rights use an original typographic placeholder instead. A cover preview does not grant permission to host the full PDF.

hosting_status_options.host: AURA may serve the local_file listed for this resource, subject to the stated license and attribution conditions.
hosting_status_options.link: Do not serve a local copy; send visitors to the official source_url.
hosting_status_options.permission-pending: Do not serve a local copy until permission is confirmed; link to source_url in the meantime.

publication_guidance.catalog_maintenance: To change a resource's button, update hosting_status and source_url. For hosting, also add local_file and place the cleared PDF at public/Resource_pdfs/<local_file>. Remove local_file when switching to link or permission-pending.
ethical_hosting: Host a complete PDF only when the applicable license permits it or the copyright holder has granted permission for public online distribution.
For works marked permission-required or rights-unverified, keep the PDF out of public/ until permission is documented; link to an official publisher or organization page instead.
Keep attribution with each resource, do not imply endorsement by the authors or publishers, and do not remove copyright or license notices.
Use non-commercial resources only in a genuinely non-commercial context, and comply with any attribution, ShareAlike, adaptation, logo, and third-party-image conditions in the stated license.
These are health and mental-health resources, not a substitute for individualized professional care. Check dates and official sources before presenting them as current guidance.
For self-harm and suicide materials, provide a content notice, avoid sensational presentation, and include support contacts appropriate to the audience's location.

resources.cover_alt: First page preview of Anxiety Disorders: An Information Guide
resources.title: Anxiety Disorders: An Information Guide

creators.name: Centre for Addiction and Mental Health (CAMH)

resources.description: CAMH patient guide on everyday anxiety versus anxiety disorders, DSM-5 categories (phobias, panic, agoraphobia, GAD, social anxiety, separation anxiety, selective mutism), causes, treatment, recovery, and family support.
resources.content_notice: If you are in an emergency or crisis, CAMH directs readers to crisis resources on its site; in Canada, 988 offers suicide and crisis support.
resources.highlights_citation: Centre for Addiction and Mental Health. Anxiety Disorders: An Information Guide (2024).
highlights: Explains how everyday worry differs from anxiety disorders that are more frequent, intense, and disruptive to work, study, and relationships.

Describes main DSM-5 categories—including panic disorder, agoraphobia, specific phobia, social anxiety disorder, GAD, separation anxiety disorder, and selective mutism—with typical thoughts, body reactions, and avoidance patterns.
Notes that anxiety disorders are common and treatable, and that early professional help improves outcomes.
Points to cognitive-behavioural approaches, recovery, relapse prevention, and support for families and friends.

rights.copyright_holder: Centre for Addiction and Mental Health (CAMH)
rights.license: All rights reserved; no general redistribution license identified.
rights.evidence: The guide states that reproduction requires written permission, except for brief quotations of up to 200 words in a review or professional work.
rights.hosting_recommendation: Do not host the full PDF publicly without written permission. Prefer linking to CAMH's official resource page.

resources.summary: CAMH 2024 guide—normal anxiety vs. disorders, DSM-5 types, treatment, recovery, and help for families.
audience: Anyone preparing to speak with a clinician about anxiety
resources.relevance: Helps name what you are experiencing, learn how disorder categories differ, and see what treatment and family support can involve.

chapters.title: Treatments for individuals with anxiety disorders

resources.title: Depression: What You Know Can Help You

creators.name: Deborah Maguire
creators.role: named in embedded PDF metadata; precise contribution should be verified

resources.description: An educational awareness packet about depression for people living with depression and their families.

rights.license: Copyrighted; the packet permits reproduction for non-commercial mental-health education and awareness activities.
rights.evidence: The packet expressly allows reproduction for non-commercial educational and awareness activities. It says permission may be requested for translation; whether public online hosting of the complete PDF is covered is not explicit.
rights.hosting_recommendation: Before hosting the complete PDF, confirm that the stated non-commercial educational permission covers public online distribution. Attribute WFMH and do not translate or adapt without permission.

resources.summary: WFMH international awareness packet on depression for people affected and their families (2010, English).

resources.cover_alt: First page preview of the NIMH Depression publication
resources.title: Depression

creators.name: National Institutes of Health, U.S. Department of Health and Human Services

resources.description: Official NIMH brochure on depression: types, signs and symptoms, diagnosis, treatment (psychotherapy, medication, brain stimulation), self-care, help for loved ones, and crisis resources.
resources.highlights_citation: National Institute of Mental Health. Depression (NIH Publication No. 24-MH-8079, Revised 2024).
resources.content_notice: NIMH notes that if you or someone you know is struggling or having thoughts of suicide, you can call or text 988 (U.S.) or chat at 988lifeline.org. In life-threatening situations, call 911.
highlights: Defines depression as persistent symptoms that affect mood, thinking, and daily activities—not the short low moods everyone has sometimes.
Describes major depression, persistent depressive disorder, seasonal and perinatal forms, and when to seek evaluation.
Outlines psychotherapy, medication, and brain stimulation options, plus self-care steps while in treatment.
Includes guidance for supporting a loved one and links to find local mental health services.

rights.copyright_holder: U.S. National Institute of Mental Health, except for any separately credited material
rights.license: The publication states that its information is in the public domain and may be reused or copied without permission; images may not be reused or copied under that notice.
rights.license_summary: Public domain text · cite NIMH · do not reuse images without permission
rights.suggested_citation: National Institute of Mental Health. (2024). Depression (NIH Publication No. 24-MH-8079). U.S. Department of Health and Human Services, National Institutes of Health.
rights.evidence: The PDF's reprints notice explicitly describes the information as public domain and excludes images. The PDF contains embedded images.
rights.hosting_recommendation: Link to NIMH's official publication page for the current PDF and web version rather than mirroring the file. Attribute NIMH when reusing text; do not reuse cover or inline images without clearance.

resources.summary: NIMH patient brochure on depression—symptoms, diagnosis, treatment, self-care, and help for loved ones (Revised 2024).
audience: People wondering if they might have depression
Family and friends supporting someone who may be depressed
resources.relevance: A plain-language U.S. federal health source you can read before an appointment; useful for recognizing symptoms and knowing what questions to ask a clinician.

resources.cover_alt: First page preview of New Oxford Textbook of Psychiatry
resources.title: New Oxford Textbook of Psychiatry (3 edn)
resources.notes: Published March 2020; Oxford Academic notes some content updated 1 January 2024.
resources.description: Third-edition Oxford textbook presenting psychiatry as a medical specialty—patient perspective, ethics, scientific bases of aetiology and treatment, and disorder chapters aligned with DSM-5, plus service provision and forensic psychiatry.
resources.highlights_citation: Geddes, J. R., Andreasen, N. C., & Goodwin, G. M. (Eds.). New Oxford Textbook of Psychiatry (3rd ed.). Oxford University Press (2020).
highlights: Frames psychiatry as a medical discipline grounded in science, phenomenology, and the patient’s perspective.
Covers diagnosis, psychopathology, evidence, and the scientific basis of aetiology and treatment.
Disorder sections follow DSM-5 structure, with additional material on genetics, imaging, and neurobiological targets.
Includes sections on service provision and forensic psychiatry as context for clinical care.

rights.copyright_holder: Oxford University Press, except for separately credited material
rights.license: All rights reserved; the book prohibits circulation in another form without prior permission, except where expressly permitted by law or license.
rights.evidence: The copyright page prohibits reproduction and circulation without permission. It identifies a government-work exception for Chapter 35 only.
rights.hosting_recommendation: Do not host the full textbook publicly without written permission. The limited Chapter 35 exception does not authorize redistribution of the book. Prefer an official publisher link.

resources.summary: Oxford’s third-edition psychiatry textbook—DSM-5–aligned disorder sections, neuroscience, ethics, and services (2020; partial updates noted 2024).
resources.relevance: Reference for disorder-level science and clinical structure when you need Oxford’s edited coverage rather than a short patient guide.
